title: Creamed Chipped Beef
subtitle: An American diner classic of dried beef in a peppery white sauce
excerpt: Thin slices of dried beef folded into a thick, peppery bechamel and served over toast. Quick to make, salty, and deeply satisfying.
sourceNotes: American military and diner staple known colloquially by many nicknames. Made with dried or salt-cured beef slices in a simple white sauce. Served over white toast.

content.text: The sauce is a standard white sauce spiked with plenty of black pepper. Dried beef is already salty, so taste before adding any extra salt. Serve the moment it is ready; the sauce thickens quickly on standing.

items.prepNote: torn or roughly chopped into small pieces
freshly ground, plus more to taste

content.text: Melt the butter in the medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and stir constantly for 2 minutes to cook out the raw taste.
Remove from the heat and gradually pour in the warm milk, whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Return to medium heat and stir until the sauce thickens and coats the back of a spoon. This takes about 5 minutes.
Add the black pepper and stir well. Taste and add salt only if needed; the beef is already salty.
Fold in the dried beef pieces. Stir gently and heat through for 2 minutes.
Toast the bread. Spoon the creamed beef over two slices per portion and serve immediately.

items.cause: The milk was added to the roux too fast, or the sauce was not whisked continuously.
items.fix: Add the milk a little at a time, whisking briskly after each addition. A blender or stick blender rescues a lumpy sauce.

items.cause: It reduced too long on the heat.
items.fix: Whisk in a splash of warm milk until it reaches a pourable, coating consistency.

items.cause: The dried beef contributed more salt than expected.
items.fix: Add more milk to dilute the sauce. Next time, rinse the beef briefly in cold water before using.
